# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-25 (Extended v178)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to spring Year 7. Primary locations include Paris—Rue Plumet (Valjean's house), Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire No. 6 (Gillenormand residence), Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of the Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue de l'Homme Armé, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven.

**Rumored claims (unverified)**: Yera Stenworth confided fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately (winter Year 5). Fenelle Lindmere and Marald confided/revealed Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (autumn Year 6).

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa later went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford, took lodgings in Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead, took lodgings in Salcombe; Fenelle Lindmere followed within month. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate, took lodgings in Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Thizek Stenenridge told Elra Corrford deed to Kelmere pastures was forged. Kassa Stenson's husband gave solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Elra Corrford gave Matho Stenson solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven.

**New births and marriages**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe with half parish present, lived in Ostcombe thereafter, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere).

**Spring Year 7 observations**: Multiple residents walked long way to avoid muddy square. Road rutted and puddled after thaw. Someone chalked crooked sun on forge wall. Multiple residents hummed childhood tunes while scrubbing steps (Yera, Rinelle, Zavus, Kadan). Matho counted coins twice, came up penny short (Elmhaven). Taric Corrley remarked river was up at Dungate crossing; Kassa Senson said it always was in spring. Ismira Stenson argued with carter over price of sack of oats (Elmhaven). Kadan Corrley and Rovus Prydenridge talked of weather, harvest, lame horse. Rovus and Kadan discussed scandal of salt prices. Yera Haskick laughed at story nobody else found funny. Yera Stenworth and Zavus complained of aching backs. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps. Children chased hoop down lane. Lurald and Ilrald discussed weather, harvest, lame horse.

## Jean Valjean's Crisis and Discovery (Night of 24th June 1832, continuing into Spring Year 7)
**Blotting-book discovery**: Upon arriving at Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings, Valjean found Cosette's blotting-book open on sideboard before mirror. Mirror reflection revealed four lines—letter Cosette had written to young workman in Rue Plumet. **Valjean's collapse**: Understood Cosette was escaping; another was goal of her heart; he was no longer anything but her father. Soul gave utter roar. **Nature of his paternal love**: Into paternity his life's widowhood introduced all shades of love—daughter, mother, sister, woman, wife. Sentiment impossible to lose—pure with blindness's purity, celestial, angelic, divine. Destinies wedded though no marriage possible. **Spiritual crisis**: Grief surpassed bounds; quiver of revolt ran head to foot; immense reawakening of egotism; the *I* howled. Profound elements crumbling—fatal crisis. **Divination**: Recognized precipice—but was at bottom. Found man instantly: unknown prowler of Luxembourg, seeker of love adventures, coward making eyes at young girl with devoted father.

**During Spring Year 7**: Groped up stairs, hand trembling greatly; thought his actions smacked of theft. Unfolded Marius's note announcing death and love. In violent emotions, seized essential points. **Transformation**: Beheld splendor of death of hated individual, remained crushed with intoxicated amazement. **Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings**: Two sleeping-rooms, dining-room, kitchen, garret for Toussaint on second floor, back court. Initially slept well; awoke almost gay; recovered serenity and security. Twice or thrice Toussaint stammered about fighting in Paris—he paid no heed, absorbed in calculations.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance (Autumn Year 5 through Evening 24th June 1832)
**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged she never forgot Marius, always loved him. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening, forcing old gate. At height of love's voluptuousness, remained absolutely chaste. **Confessions (spring Year 6, during cholera)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, father colonel and hero on bad terms with rich grandfather, hinted at being baron. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent. **Éponine's death (evening 24th June)**: Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade, spoke of her death as blessing, protected him from gunfire. Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying. **Cosette's letter content**: Marriage impossible; grandfather refuses; no fortune either; hastened to him, he gone; kept promise given; dies; loves him. **Marius's response**: Covered letter with kisses; reflected Cosette going to England, nothing changed. Resolved to inform Cosette of death, send farewell, save Gavroche.

**Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans England departure in one week, arranged meeting 26th June at nine o'clock. Same evening, displaced bar at grating, rushed in. Cosette absent. Seated self with resolution, blessed love, said all left was to die. Mad with grief, one desire: speedy end. Voice summoned him to barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie. **Philosophy of duty**: Reflected on Colonel Pontmercy—proud soldier, guarded frontier, touched Asia, beheld cities, left blood, returned after twenty years scarred but pure. Own day come; must follow father, show bravery, seek death. Carries loaded pistols. **During first phase**: Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed; flung self into conflict. Saved Gavroche with first shot, delivered Courfeyrac with second. Seized powder barrel, glided along barricade to cage of paving-stones with torch, tore torch, replaced with powder barrel, stood foot on stones with torch in hand, dropped flame with startling cry. **Mental state (6th June, dawn)**: Fasting, fevered, emerged from all hope, stranded in grief, saturated with violent emotions, conscious end was near, plunged into visionary stupor preceding fatal hour voluntarily accepted. Suffering's voluptuousness. Despair's ecstasy. Looked on at everything as from without; things seemed far away; beheld men as through flame; heard voices as at bottom of abyss. Under shadow of great, dark wings spread over those in death agony. Felt he had entered tomb, already on other side of wall, beheld faces of living with eyes of one dead. This attitude of M. Fauchelevent comforting to him; found absolute impossibility of addressing that enigmatical man, who was equivocal and imposing. Long time since seen him.

## Barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie (Evening 24th June 1832, into morning 6th June)
**Café Corinthe**: Ground floor with bar; first floor with billiard-table and wooden spiral staircase; cellar via trap-door; lodgings and attics. Proprietor: Widow Hucheloup. Serving-maids: Matelote, Gibelotte. **Two barricades**: Larger shut off Rue de la Chanvrerie; other closed Rue Mondétour. **Larger barricade (6th June, dawn)**: Height six or seven feet, stepped construction, paling-stones, casks, wheels, omnibus pole with ropes, red flag. Forty-three insurgents commanded by Enjolras, Combeferre, Courfeyrac, etc. Six commanded by Feuilly at windows with guns. **Three-front fortification (6th June)**: Walled on Rue de la Chanvrerie (front), Rues du Cygne and de la Petite Truanderie (left), Rue Mondétour (right). Small gut of Mondétour lane barricaded after pavement torn up for length of several houses. Really almost impregnable but fatally hemmed in—fortress but rat hole too. Three fronts, no exit.

**Javert's arrest**: Identified as Inspector of Police, aged fifty-two. Card, watch, purse with gold, sealed envelope with five lines in Prefect's handwriting discovered. Bound with whip-cord about feet (steps fifteen inches length), martingale rope from neck forking on stomach, meeting hands after passing between legs. Upon seeing Valjean surveying him, did not start, dropped lids proudly, remarked: "It is perfectly simple."

**Le Cabuc execution**: Enjolras executed him for killing, justified by insurrection needing discipline. Tradition: Le Cabuc was Claquesous.

**M. Mabeuf's sacrifice**: Venerable, austere, sold unique Diogenes Laertius, returned with hundred francs. Evening 24th June: followed band, refused arms. During attack: at detonation, tore flag from Enjolras. Eighty years old, white locks, aged arm upholding red banner. Enjolras eulogized: magnificent death; presence renders barricade impregnable. Father Mabeuf's body lay in kitchen on table; wine bottles placed under table to prevent Grantaire from drinking.

**Unknown young figure**: Pale, thin, small, freckled, youthful artisan in tattered blouse and patched velvet trousers; spoke to Courfeyrac in peculiar voice. During attack: hand laid on muzzle when soldier aimed at Marius, shot traversed hand, artisan possibly struck and fell, but ball did not hit Marius.

**Unknown messenger (6th June, dawn)**: Some unknown blouse-wearer appeared, stranger and passing hero, announced with inexorable resolution: whole army of Paris striking, third of army bearing down, National Guard advancing, shakos of fifth line and standards of sixth legion visible, attack in one hour, no populace stirring, nothing to expect, abandoned. Never known name of this man who vanished into shadows.

**After first assault and repairs**: Insurgents rallied, majority ascended to first-story window, commanded assailants. Medical students cared for wounded. Five gravely wounded men on mattresses in kitchen converted to ambulance; two municipal guardsmen attended. Barricade repaired and augmented, raised two feet. Bars of iron planted resembled lances in rest. Redoubt cleverly made over into wall on inside, thicket on outside.

**Provisions and morale (6th June, dawn)**: No repast possible. Neither bread nor meat. Fifty men exhausted scanty provisions during sixteen hours. **Wine cache**: Fifteen full bottles hermetically sealed found in cellar. Enjolras placed veto on them. **Insurgent resolve**: Insurgents full of hope, smiled waiting for dawn attack, no doubt as to success or cause, reckoned succor on way, divided day into three phases: six o'clock—regiment would turn; noon—insurrection of all Paris; sunset—revolution.

**Preparation for assault (6th June morning)**: Enjolras paused rather than became silent; lips continued to move silently as though talking to himself. All gazed attentively. No applause; whispered together for long time. Speech being breath, rustling of intelligences resembles rustling of leaves. Heroic men began to denounce each other about which should not be placed at door of tomb—each struggled to determine which should not allow himself placed at door. Young man told full-grown man: "You are father of family. Go." Man retorted: "Your duty rather; you have two sisters whom you maintain." Unprecedented controversy broke forth. **Sentinel**: Stationed by insurgents in Rue Mondétour allowed National Guardsman to entangle himself in street, saying to self: "Probably it is reinforcement, in any case it is prisoner." Moment too grave to admit abandoning duty and observation post. **Barricade discipline**: Each man selects place as though at theatre. Left-handed men precious. Many arrange to fight in sitting posture. Nothing more curious than barricade preparing for assault. As soon as leader gives order to clear decks for action, all disorderly movements cease; everything in spirits converges into waiting for assailants. Barricade before danger is chaos; in danger, discipline itself. Peril produces order. **Dawn scene**: Daylight increasing rapidly. Not window opened, not door ajar—dawn but not awaking. End of Rue de la Chanvrerie evacuated by troops, seemed free, presented sinister tranquillity. Rue Saint-Denis dumb as avenue of Sphinxes at Thebes. Not living being in crossroads gleaming white in sun's light. Nothing mournful as this light in deserted streets. Nothing seen, but something heard—mysterious movement at distance. Critical moment approaching. All sentinels had come in.

## Philosophical Discussions (6th June, barricade)
Combeferre quoted and discussed classical figures—Harmodius and Aristogiton, Brutus, Chereas, Stephanus, Cromwell, Charlotte Corday, Sand—noting their moments of agony and remorse at striking men even for liberation. Compared translators of Georgics—Raux, Cournand, Delille, Malfilâtre—particularly prodigies of Cæsar's death. Discussion reverted to Brutus through mention of Cæsar. Combeferre argued Cæsar fell justly; severity toward Cæsar not diatribe but just arbitration in thought as Brutus's arbiter by sword. Noted Cæsar violated Rubicon, conferred dignities as though from himself, not rising at senate entrance, committed acts of king and tyrant. His twenty-three wounds touch less than spitting in face of Jesus Christ. Cæsar stabbed by senators; Christ cuffed by lackeys. One feels God through greater outrage.
